title: TESS periods from 2018 to 2026 do not continue SuperWASP period-change rates of 511 short-period eclipsing binaries: changes are 7 times smaller than secular extrapolation and reverse within decades
abstract: Question: Do the SuperWASP (about 2004-2012) orbital period-change rates of Lohr et al. (2015, 697 'linear' binaries; 2013, 143 short-period binaries) predict the TESS periods measured about 14 years later? Method: We matched the 1SWASP sources to TIC stars, timed eclipses in 2,802 TESS light curves (QLP, TESS-SPOC, SPOC) with a Fourier template per orbit segment, counted cycles with local sector periods in half-cycle units, and compared P(TESS) - P(SuperWASP) with the secular prediction rate x (t_TESS - 2008.5). Results: For 511 unique stars, the observed differences are 0.15 times the predicted size. The Theil-Sen slope is 0.026 (95% 0.013-0.044), and only 10% of the stars agree with the prediction at 3 sigma. Mid-epochs of 2006.5 and 2010.5 give the same result. But 83% of the periods did change significantly, with no common offset, and the signs agree in 61% of the cases. The mean rate over the gap (median |rate|/P = 0.39e-6 per yr) is 7 times smaller than the SuperWASP rate (2.7e-6 per yr). TESS-only rates have a similar size (1.2e-6 per yr) but do not correlate with the SuperWASP rates (r = -0.01). The size of the later change is the same for the 'linear', 'sinusoidal' and insignificant classes. Sinusoidal O-C populations with modulation periods of about 3-40 yr agree with the data; populations dominated by periods above about 50 yr, or by secular change, do not. Of the three 2012 merger candidates, only J133105.91+121538.0 continues to decrease (-0.235 s, P/Pdot about 1 Myr). Limitations: The SuperWASP reference epoch is assumed (2008.5 +- 2 yr). We did not re-measure the SuperWASP times. TESS-only rates use 3-6 sectors. We cannot separate light-travel-time from magnetic causes. display.caption: Observed TESS minus SuperWASP period against the secular prediction (Lohr et al. rate x time from 2008.5), symmetric-log axes. Left: 511 stars of the Lohr et al. (2015) linear table. Right: 34 stars of the Lohr et al. (2013) short-period table with a rate. The orange line is the secular prediction; most stars fall near zero instead.

Fractional period-change rates (dP/dt / P, log bins, both signs): SuperWASP rates (orange), mean rate from SuperWASP to TESS (blue, 7 times smaller), and rates inside the TESS interval at sector level (green, similar in size to SuperWASP but uncorrelated with it).

Theil-Sen slope (left) and size ratio (right) predicted by populations of sinusoidal O-C changes with log-uniform modulation periods, without and with selection plus rate noise, against the observed values (green; band = bootstrap 16-84%). Modulation periods of about 3-40 yr fit; populations dominated by periods above about 50 yr do not.

citations.reason: Lohr et al. 2015: SuperWASP period-change rates tested here; we find that the rates do not continue and that long-period third-body cycles do not fit.
Lohr et al. 2013: 143 short-period SuperWASP binaries and their rates, tested with TESS.
Lohr et al. 2012: three period-decrease merger candidates; one continues to decrease.
Lohr et al. 2013b: cyclic period change of J234401.81-212229.1, which agrees with our TESS period.
